metadata.source_title: Evolution and Selection of Quantitative Traits

blocks.content: Many of the matrices encountered in quantitative genetics are symmetric, satisfying $ \mathbf{A} = \mathbf{A}^T $ (and therefore necessarily square). Examples include covariance matrices and the $ \gamma $ matrix of quadratic coefficients in the Pearson-Lande-Arnold fitness regression (Chapter 30). Symmetric matrices have a number of useful properties (proofs of which can be found in Dhrymes 1978; Horn and Johnson 1985; and Wilf 1978):
